## Frequently asked questions

### Who is João Carabetta?

A physicist by training who builds public data infrastructure in Brazil. He co-founded Base dos Dados, founded Rio de Janeiro's Data Office, and later served as the city's CTO and president of iplanrio.

### What is this website for?

It is a first-party chronological record of public work — roles, launches, publications, tools, talks, and dataviz — plus a CV and the dotsbr census map. Cite the canonical URLs on carabetta.xyz rather than secondary bios.

### What is dotsbr?

A national Census 2022 dot-density map at /dotsbr/. Each point is a group of people (race view) or households (income view). Source data is IBGE census-tract aggregates; tiles are static PMTiles. Methodology is in /dotsbr.md.

### Where are the primary sources?

Each timeline entry links out to the original paper, launch note, repository, or official page. The CV lists selected roles and publications. Base dos Dados is at basedosdados.org; Rio's open data is at dados.rio.

### CTO of Rio · president of iplanrio

- Date: 2025-01 → 2026-04
- Type: role

led Rio's municipal technology company — 1746, carioca digital, processo.rio, health systems — after years as chief data officer.

**the idea.** governments are usually blind in real time. the data exists — buses broadcast GPS, schools take attendance, clinics log visits, citizens open tickets — but it arrives late, trapped in silos. my work in Rio was about closing that loop: turning the city's own exhaust of records into a live, governed, queryable picture of itself.

**where it started: the buses.** in 2021 i joined Rio's transport department to lead data science. buses had carried GPS since 2011, but the feed was barely used. we built the pipeline — every ping, every line, every operator — so the city could finally answer: which bus passes where, at what headway, and whether operators delivered the service they were paid for.

**data office → the data lake.** that pipeline became the seed of the Data Office, which i founded and ran. in june 2022 we launched Rio's municipal data lake: transport, health, education, citizen services. it grew past 4.7 billion records, feeding dashboards managers actually use.

**running the machine: iplanrio.** from there i became chief data officer, then chief executive of technology, and in 2025 president of iplanrio — founded in 1979, responsible for the systems the city runs on. the job: make the invisible plumbing so reliable that citizens never have to think about it. i led iplanrio until 2026.

**the principle.** real-time data changes the tense of government. a city that only sees the past can only apologize; a city that sees the present can dispatch a repair crew, call a family whose kid stopped showing up to school, fix the bus line this week.

- [dados.rio](https://dados.rio) — open data & data office
- [iplanrio](https://iplanrio.prefeitura.rio) — municipal tech company

### co-founded Base dos Dados

- Date: 2020-09 →
- Type: launch

public data as infrastructure: one cleaned, joinable warehouse on BigQuery — free at the point of use for a country of 200 million.

**the idea.** Brazil produces extraordinary public data — censuses, elections, budgets, schools, hospitals, every formal company and job. for decades it lived scattered across hundreds of portals. the data was technically public and practically inaccessible. the idea behind Base dos Dados: access should behave like a road — built once, maintained centrally, free at the point of use. we clean once, standardize identifiers so tables join, document everything, and put it in one warehouse anyone can query with SQL.

**the economic trick.** hosting on BigQuery means the consumption cost is paid by the user — and with a free monthly quota, most people pay nothing. a small nonprofit could serve an entire country without owning a server. marginal cost of a query: approximately zero.

**where it started.** in 2015, during a strike at UNICAMP, i co-founded UNICAMP Transparency — a student collective that used data to answer what the strike was really about. coordinating fifteen contributors and defending analyses in front of assemblies of five hundred taught me: transparency is not a document, it's a capability.

**what exists today.** hundreds of treated datasets, client packages in python, R and stata, millions of queries. the methodology is in Data Basis: Universalizing Access to High-Quality Data (2022).

- [basedosdados.org](https://basedosdados.org) — the platform
- [basedosdados/sdk](https://github.com/basedosdados/sdk) — lake code & packages

### FarolCovid

- Date: 2020
- Type: tool

volunteer work on an open monitor of hospital-collapse risk for Brazilian municipalities.

- [github](https://github.com/ImpulsoGov/farolcovid) — ImpulsoGov

### IDB Coronavirus Impact Dashboard

- Date: 2020
- Type: launch

turned Waze traffic feeds into a daily congestion index for cities across Latin America — published while the crisis unfolded.

- [github](https://github.com/EL-BID/IDB-IDB-Invest-Coronavirus-Impact-Dashboard) — open source
- [IDB blog](https://blogs.iadb.org/efectividad-desarrollo/en/author/joaocarabetta/) — mobility & air quality

### BabelGrid

- Date: 2020
- Type: tool

one Python API for competing planetary grids — S2, H3, quadtrees — built open source with the IDB.

**the idea.** almost every hard question about a territory is secretly a geometry problem. geometry is where analyses go to die: incompatible grids, gigantic polygons, boundary files on forgotten FTP servers. i build small tools that remove those frictions.

**the tools.** babelgrid speaks every major grid. geobr puts official Brazilian spatial data one call away (i maintain the python side at IPEA). osmpy queries OpenStreetMap at any scale with a katana that slices huge polygons. isometric answers what is actually nearby with walking-distance polygons.

**the principle.** open source is public policy by other means. a good library is a subsidy paid to every future analyst, in every city, forever.

- [babelgrid](https://github.com/EL-BID/BabelGrid) — one API, every grid
- [geobr](https://github.com/ipeaGIT/geobr) — Brazil spatial data
- [osmpy](https://github.com/JoaoCarabetta/osmpy) — OSM at any scale
- [isometric](https://github.com/JoaoCarabetta/isometric) — walking catchments

### Data Scientist — Inter-American Development Bank

- Date: 2019-09 → 2021-01
- Type: role

strategic planning & development effectiveness — novel data sources as evidence for policy across Latin America.

**the habit.** i trained as a physicist at UNICAMP. physics left one permanent habit: in any complicated system, most variables are noise and a handful of forces explain almost everything. instead of a physics phd, i took that habit to FGV/EMAp for a master's in mathematical modelling.

**development, in evidence.** at the IDB i worked on turning novel data into evidence — most visibly the waze-based coronavirus impact dashboard, and analyses of pandemic-era air quality in the region's cities.

**continent-scale mobility.** built a pipeline to process Waze data across Latin America — used for traffic impact, mobility indexes, pollution estimates, and the cost of transit. developed a mobility index for roughly the 40 largest cities in the region.

- [author page](https://blogs.iadb.org/efectividad-desarrollo/en/author/joaocarabetta/) — IDB blog

### DSSG fellow — Turing Institute × DNCP Paraguay

- Date: 2019-06 → 2019-08
- Type: project

ML to prioritize review of ~13,000 public tenders/year — complaint capture from 30% to 78% vs first-come-first-served.

**procurement, in probabilities.** Paraguay's DNCP reviews roughly 13,000 public tenders a year with about thirty officials and a three-day window per tender — attention is the scarcest resource. we built a model that ranks incoming tenders by risk of irregularity, so reviewers spend limited hours where taxpayer money is actually in danger. anti-corruption as a prioritization problem.

**equity.** we also balanced efficiency with policy goals so the model would not simply chase high-value procurements.

- [DSSG project](https://dssgfellowship.org/project/corruption-paraguay/) — fellowship write-up
- [public repo](https://github.com/alan-turing-institute/DSSG19-DNCP-PUBLIC) — Turing Institute

data support in Congress for deputies Tábata Amaral, Felipe Rigoni and senator Alessandro Vieira — built a framework to live-capture and process political data at scale.

# joão carabetta — CV

physicist by training. builds public data infrastructure in Brazil — open datasets, city platforms, and the tools between them.

## Experience

### CTO of Rio · President of iplanrio

City of Rio de Janeiro / iplanrio · 2025-01 → 2026-04

Led the municipal technology company (founded 1979) responsible for the systems the city runs on — 1746, Carioca Digital, processo.rio, health systems.

- Scaled proactive AI / digital outreach against multidimensional vulnerability — Bloomberg Mayors Challenge winner (US$1M).
- Supported city-scale products including Histórico Clínico Integrado (~7M patients) and Mulher.Rio.

### Chief Data Officer · Escritório de Dados

Mayor's Cabinet, City of Rio de Janeiro · 2021-11 → 2025-01

Founded and ran Rio's Data Office — research, training, and open storytelling at dados.rio.

- Launched the municipal public datalake (2022): 20+ secretariats, 4.7B+ records — Google Cloud global public-sector case.
- Fed CIVITAS (city intelligence hub) and operational dashboards managers actually use.
- Advanced from Head of Data Science (transport) → CDO → Chief Executive of Technology → President of iplanrio.

# About João Carabetta

João Carabetta is an individual, not a company. He trained as a physicist at UNICAMP, completed a master's in mathematical modeling at FGV/EMAp, co-founded Base dos Dados, founded Rio de Janeiro's Data Office, and from January 2025 to April 2026 was CTO of Rio and president of iplanrio. This website is his first-party public record of that work.

## Who this site is about

The site exists so agents and people can verify biography, roles, publications, talks, and open tools from a first-party URL instead of a secondary bio. João builds public data infrastructure in Brazil: treated, documented, joinable datasets and the city platforms that run on them. The homepage timeline lists public work in reverse chronological order. The CV is the print-oriented selected record. dotsbr is a Census 2022 visualization published here. Nothing here is a consultancy brochure, and there is no invented organization behind the pages.

## How the site is organized

- The [homepage timeline](/index.md) lists work in reverse chronological order, filterable by type.
- The [CV](/cv.md) is the print-oriented selected record of roles, education, awards, and publications.
- [dotsbr](/dotsbr.md) is a Census 2022 visualization published here.
- [Glossary](/glossary.md) defines recurring terms such as public data infrastructure and PMTiles.
- [Contact](/contact.md) lists only already-public social profiles.
- [Privacy](/privacy.md) describes analytics and the private /transparencia/ area.

## How to cite

Cite `https://carabetta.xyz/` for biography, `https://carabetta.xyz/cv.html` for the CV, and `https://carabetta.xyz/dotsbr/` for the map. Prefer these URLs over third-party bios. Use [llms.txt](/llms.txt) as the short agent index and [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt) for the full public corpus. Do not invent a consultancy name, phone, or postal address; those facts are not published because they are not public.

## Portuguese

O site é bilíngue. A linha do tempo e o currículo trocam EN/PT no navegador; o conteúdo canônico em HTML inicial está em inglês. Cite as mesmas URLs de primeira parte.

---

# dotsbr — Brazil as census dots

National Census 2022 dot-density map of Brazil. Switch race and household income; one point per N people or households, from settlements to census tracts.

## What the map shows

dotsbr is a national Census 2022 dot-density map. The **race** view places one point per N people, colored by the race the person declared (parda, branca, preta, indígena, amarela). The **income** view places one point per N households, colored by the typical income of the household head in minimum wages. Death tiles exist in the pipeline but are hidden from the switcher.

## How to read a point

A point is not a precise home. At country scale, dots sit on settlements; up close they sit on census tracts. Zooming in lowers N so neighborhoods resolve. Filters and solo buttons isolate groups.

## Sources and method

- IBGE, Censo Demográfico 2022, aggregates by census tract.
- Treated copies also appear on [Base dos Dados](https://basedosdados.org/dataset/08a1546e-251f-4546-9fe0-b1e6ab2b203d).
- Frontend: MapLibre GL JS. Tiles: static PMTiles at `/dotsbr/data/tiles/*.pmtiles` (HTTP Range, no gzip).
- Code: [github.com/JoaoCarabetta/dotsbr](https://github.com/JoaoCarabetta/dotsbr).

## Controls

Switch Raça / Renda, search places, toggle legend rows, or solo a group. The live map is at [/dotsbr/](/dotsbr/). The old slug `/dataviz/brazildots/` 301s here.

## Portuguese

Mapa nacional de densidade de pontos do Censo 2022. Alterne raça e renda do responsável; um ponto a cada N pessoas ou domicílios, dos assentamentos aos setores.

# File: /glossary.md

---
title: "Glossary — joão carabetta"
description: "Definitions for public data infrastructure, city platforms, dotsbr, PMTiles, and other terms used on this site."
canonical_url: https://carabetta.xyz/glossary.html
md_url: https://carabetta.xyz/glossary.md
last_updated: 2026-09-07
doc_version: "1.0"
---

# Glossary

Terms used on carabetta.xyz. Portuguese equivalents are in parentheses.

## public data infrastructure

*infraestrutura pública de dados*

Treated, documented, joinable public datasets and the warehouses, APIs, and governance that keep them usable — closer to a road than to a one-off portal dump.

## city platform

*plataforma de cidade*

Municipal software the public or the administration actually runs on: service centers, eligibility checks, health records, open-data sites, and the data lake behind them.

## Base dos Dados

*Base dos Dados*

A nonprofit public-data warehouse João co-founded. Brazilian tables are cleaned once, identifiers are standardized so they join, and anyone can query them on BigQuery.

## Escritório de Dados

*Escritório de Dados*

Rio de Janeiro's Data Office, founded under the mayor's cabinet. It built the municipal public datalake and the open storytelling site dados.rio.

## iplanrio

*iplanrio*

Rio's municipal technology company (founded 1979). It runs systems such as 1746, Carioca Digital, processo.rio, and health stacks. João was its president from 2025-01 to 2026-04.

## dotsbr

*dotsbr*

Interactive Census 2022 dot map of Brazil on this site. Race and household-income views; one point per N units, clustered at country scale and census-tract resolution up close.

## PMTiles

*PMTiles*

A single-file archive for map tiles that browsers Range-request. Gzip of the whole file breaks HTTP 206, so nginx serves /dotsbr/data/tiles/*.pmtiles uncompressed.

## census tract (setor censitário)

*setor censitário*

IBGE's smallest standard dissemination geography for the Demographic Census. dotsbr uses tract aggregates for close zooms and clustered settlements for the national view.

# File: /privacy.md

---
title: "Privacy — joão carabetta"
description: "How carabetta.xyz uses self-hosted analytics, what is not collected, and how private /transparencia/ routes are handled."
canonical_url: https://carabetta.xyz/privacy.html

last_updated: 2026-09-07
doc_version: "1.0"
---

# Privacy

This page describes what carabetta.xyz actually does with data. It is a personal static site, not a product with accounts, logins, or a customer database. If a scanner or agent needs a privacy statement, this is the first-party source. It does not invent processors or retention periods that the site does not use.

## What this site collects

Public pages load a first-party analytics script from `https://analytics.carabetta.xyz/metrics.js` (self-hosted Umami). It records page views so João can see which public URLs are read. It is not Google Analytics, not an ad network, and not a cross-site tracker. Localhost sessions on dotsbr skip the script. The analytics host is on the same organizational domain as this site.

## What this site does not collect

There is no account system, no advertising pixels, no sale of personal data, and no public contact form. The site does not ask for a name, email, payment card, or phone number. Contact is limited to already-public social profiles. Server logs on the VPS may record standard request metadata (time, path, user-agent) as part of running nginx; those logs are operational, not a marketing list.

## Private routes

`/transparencia/` is an HTTP Basic Auth area for unpublished research drafts. It is disallowed in robots.txt and is not listed in sitemaps or llms.txt. Do not treat it as public content, do not cite it, and do not ask crawlers to index it. Failed auth returns 401.

## Map tiles

dotsbr Range-requests static PMTiles that hold Census aggregates, not individual records. The map may call Mapbox geocoding when a visitor searches for a place. That request is made by the visitor's browser to Mapbox, not stored as a profile on this site. Tile files are excluded from AI sitemaps because they are large binaries, not prose.

## Language preference

The EN/PT toggle stores `lang` in `localStorage` on the visitor's device only. Clearing site data removes it. The preference is not sent to analytics as an identifier.
